title: Look E pilot: Character Bible, rules-9 card templates and two pilot characters
problem: Owner brief: a polished Kickstarter tabletop edition, then the phone game, with a reusable art pipeline a solo developer can run. Today's printed portraits are 16x16 pixel faces about 21-26 mm wide, the Drive print kit is rules version 8, and there is no art manifest, style lock or print template with bleed.
scope: Character Bible v0.1 (docs/art/CHARACTER_BIBLE.md): one line per character for all 45 plus the walk-in figure, full entries and master prompts for Benny and Sailor Jia Wen; stop for approval

Rules-9 card templates for customer, guest and shopkeeper fronts, filled from src/engine/data.ts, with bleed, crop marks and an empty portrait window; home-print and factory PDFs from a new print script; no game code change
Pilot concepts: three directions per pilot with prompts and scoring; the owner picks one each
Pilot masters: master reference, front, three-quarter and side views, six expressions, a person's clean-up, script checks (palette, line, transparency), manifest entries
QA (eight scores, each at least 4/5), a 100% print test, and a phone mock-up beside today's pixel look; style-lock sheet for approval
exclusions: Any change to rules, balance, card text, saves, online play or the app's screens
Generating the whole roster; characters beyond the two pilots
Spending money (image tools, artists, proofs) without a dated quote and the owner's separate approval
Publishing anything, including a Kickstarter page

acceptance.text: Character Bible approved by the owner
Card templates print at 100% with bleed and crop marks; the densest card (three order lines) fits; customer backs differ only by fruit icons
Both pilots score at least 4/5 in all eight QA categories, with the evidence recorded
Hidden-information check: no type cue in either pilot; the cue-balance table is recorded
Every pilot asset has a manifest row (tool, version, date, references, prompt, human changes, approval)
